title: Optimize quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) + smoothquant folding + dequant fusion; KV-cache & continuous-batching scheduler tweaks
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for quantized inference paths (INT8 and FP8) while preserving model quality. This PR implements a set of runtime-level optimizations: 1) fused dequantization and matmul kernel for INT8/FP8 inference to eliminate redundant memory traffic and reduce activation roundtrips; 2) a static folding pass that applies SmoothQuant-compatible scale folding into quant params at model load time; 3) a lightweight KV-cache dequant fusion path that avoids per-step dequant/requant when serving with warmed caches; 4) scheduler improvements for continuous batching that expose higher utilization without increasing 99th percentile latency. Changes are implemented with targeted unit tests, microbenchmarks, and a canary rollout plan.

benchmark-suite: measured on p4d.24xlarge - see performance_summary field
performance_summary: Microbenchmarks (p4d.24xlarge, single-GPU): INT8 fused path: token throughput +22% (seq_len=1024, batch=4) and 99th-pctl latency -12%. FP8 fused path: throughput +18% and 99th-pctl latency -10%. KV-cache dequant fusion: additional +10% token throughput for long-history chat workloads (seq_len=2048) and eliminated ~30% of redundant memory copies. Continuous-batching scheduler: end-to-end tail latency reduced by 15% under 80-95th percentile load patterns. Memory: effective activation memory reduction ~8-12% enabling ~1-2 more concurrent contexts per A100 40GB equivalent. Quality: automated accuracy checks (per Linear ENG-4219 prompts) show <0.3% change in logprobs on average and no semantic regressions detected.
rollback_plan: Canary rollout for 24h on dedicated cluster (dev->staging->canary) with perf/latency monitors and automatic rollback if 99th-pctl latency regresses >5% or accuracy drift >1% on eval sets.
release_notes: Performance: Optimized quantized inference kernels (INT8/FP8) with fused dequant+matmul, SmoothQuant folding at model load, KV-cache dequant fusion, and scheduler improvements for continuous batching. Result is lower latency and higher throughput for quantized models; recommended for customers using INT8/FP8 serving.
